meta.scope: What tax, if any, is imposed on the inheritance itself at the federal, state, and local level. Distinct from the property tax reassessment covered on the Property Tax Law page.
meta.privacy: No estate size, donor identity, or beneficiary identity is stored. The owner indicated the cash portion of the inheritance 'could be over the amount that is allowed' without giving a figure, so the threshold tables are published as thresholds rather than as an applied calculation.

rows.label: Basic exclusion amount (estate and gift) for a decedent dying in calendar year 2026
rows.note: OBBBA section 70106 amended IRC 2010(c)(3) to set the basic exclusion amount at $15,000,000 for calendar year 2026. There is no scheduled sunset.

rows.label: Basic exclusion amount for a decedent dying in calendar year 2025
rows.source_name: IRS, Estate tax — filing threshold for year of death
rows.note: Published in the IRS estate tax filing-threshold table.

rows.label: Basic exclusion amount for a decedent dying in calendar year 2024
rows.source_name: IRS, Estate tax — filing threshold for year of death
rows.note: Published in the IRS estate tax filing-threshold table.

rows.label: Is the $15,000,000 amount indexed after 2026?
rows.value: Yes — adjusted for inflation for calendar year 2027 and future years
rows.note: Verbatim: 'These numbers are adjusted for inflation for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2026. The basic exclusion amount will be adjusted for inflation for calendar year 2027 and future years.'

rows.label: Generation-skipping transfer tax exemption for calendar year 2026
rows.note: IRC 2631(c). Equal to the basic exclusion amount. Not portable between spouses and must be allocated.

rows.label: Can a surviving spouse use a deceased spouse's unused exclusion?
rows.value: Yes — by election on a timely filed estate tax return
rows.note: Verbatim: 'Beginning January 1, 2011, estates of decedents survived by a spouse may elect to pass any of the decedent's unused exemption to the surviving spouse. This election is made on a timely filed estate tax return for the decedent with a surviving spouse.' A return is required even for an estate far below the threshold if portability is wanted.

rows.label: Form 706 filing test
rows.value: Required when the gross estate, increased by adjusted taxable gifts and specific gift tax exemption, exceeds the filing threshold for the year of death
rows.note: The threshold equals the basic exclusion amount for the year of death — $15,000,000 for 2026.

rows.label: Income tax basis of property acquired from a decedent
rows.value: Fair market value at the date of death (stepped-up basis)
rows.source_name: IRS Publication 551, Basis of Assets (Rev. December 2025), 'Inherited Property'
rows.note: This is the single most important number for the sell-versus-hold decision. If Property C is sold shortly after the date of death, the gain above the date-of-death value is near zero, so the federal and California capital gain on the appreciation that occurred during the decedent's lifetime is never taxed. IRS also notes IRC 1014(f) consistency rules and final regulations under T.D. 9991.

rows.label: California estate tax currently payable
rows.value: Zero — the tax is a pick-up tax measured only by the federal Credit for State Death Taxes, which Congress repealed
rows.source_name: California Legislative Information, Revenue and Taxation Code section 13302
rows.note: Statute text: 'whenever a federal estate tax is payable to the United States, there is hereby imposed a California estate tax equal to the portion, if any, of the maximum allowable amount of the Credit for State Death Taxes...' With no federal credit to pick up, the California tax computes to zero. Flagged: the federal repeal citation (EGTRRA, effective for deaths after 2004-12-31) was not separately retrieved from an official source in this pass.

rows.label: California inheritance tax payable by the beneficiary
rows.note: LEFT BLANK ON PURPOSE. Widely reported as none, because Proposition 6 repealed the state inheritance tax in 1982, but this session did not retrieve an official California source stating that, so no value is asserted here. Confirm with the Franchise Tax Board before relying on it. The practical conclusion that no California death tax is currently collected is independently supported by R&T Code 13302 above, which is verified, and by the absence of any other death-tax statute in Division 2, Part 8 of the Revenue and Taxation Code.

rows.label: City or county estate or inheritance tax in Cupertino or San Francisco
rows.note: No official source located confirming the absence of a local death tax. Leave blank until confirmed. Note separately that San Francisco does impose a one-time documentary transfer tax on recorded transfers, which is a different tax and is listed on the Inheritance Process page.

rows.label: Maximum federal long-term capital gains rate
rows.note: Not retrieved from an official IRS source in this pass. The 2026 rate tables are in Rev. Proc. 2025-32 but the long-term capital gains rate structure was not confirmed line by line. Needed for the sell-and-reinvest scenario's after-tax return; shown there as an assumption instead.

rows.label: California tax rate on capital gains
rows.note: California taxes capital gains as ordinary income, but the applicable bracket percentages were not retrieved from the Franchise Tax Board in this pass. Shown as an assumption on Methodology.

rows.label: Annual gift tax exclusion per donee, 2026
rows.note: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 sets this figure, but the session only verified section 2.14 (the basic exclusion amount) line by line. Confirm before use.

threshold_projection.description: Projection of the federal basic exclusion amount. The 2026 figure is verified. Every later year is a projection and is labelled as such. The indexing method is set by statute (IRC 2010(c)(3)(B)); the assumed rate is a modelling input, not a fact.
threshold_projection.indexing_note: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 states the amount 'will be adjusted for inflation for calendar year 2027 and future years.' The statutory index was not retrieved from the U.S. Code in this pass, so the growth rate below is an assumption.
